comments.body:
Reviewed this — the fix itself is correct: swapping the full `input.value = text` overwrite for `setRangeText(..., selectionStart, selectionEnd, "end")` is the right API, it only replaces the current selection, and the target (`<input type="text">` in `_queries.html.erb`) fully supports it. No functional issues found.

One thing worth a look: the new test `"moves the cursor after the pasted text and updates the submit label"` asserts `selectionStart`/`selectionEnd` === `5` after pasting `"x\ny"` at position 1 in `"ab"`. Per the HTML spec, `setRangeText(replacement, start, end, "end")` should land the cursor at `start + replacement.length` = `1 + 3` = **4** (right after the pasted `"x;y"`, before the trailing `"b"`).

I verified this diverges from spec because of a bug in `happy-dom` (the vitest DOM environment here, v21.0.4 — currently the latest release): `HTMLInputElement.setRangeText` computes `newEnd = start + this.value.length` (length of the whole *post-replacement* value) instead of `start + replacement.length`, which happens to clamp to `5` in this case. I couldn't find this filed upstream (`capricorn86/happy-dom`), and there's no newer happy-dom version to pick up — 21.0.4 is latest.

So this isn't a regression in the app, and it doesn't block merging — the shipped behavior is correct in real browsers. But the test's hardcoded `5` only passes because it mirrors the mock DOM's bug rather than verifying the actual "cursor right after the pasted text" behavior described in the PR. Worth changing that assertion to `4` (or asserting position relative to the replacement's end rather than a hardcoded absolute index) so the test doesn't silently start failing if happy-dom ever fixes this, and so it actually checks what it claims to check.
